_comment: Copy to config.json in ~/.claude/brink/ and edit. The kill switch is a fixed path: create ~/.claude/brink/DISABLED to instantly disable Brink.
_projection_comment: Burn-rate projection (default ON). At each pre-tool check, if usage is within `headroom` points of the pause threshold AND the sustained burn rate (measured over at least min_span_sec of same-window sensor history) projects past the threshold within lookahead_min, Brink pauses pre-emptively - a few minutes early beats hitting the hard limit inside a long tool call, where no check runs and no pause is possible. Set enabled:false to pause only on the raw thresholds. The rate is measured over the OBSERVED interval (oldest sample -> the reading's updated_at) and then carried across the blind interval (updated_at -> now) to estimate where the meter stands now; headroom and the projection are judged on that estimate. blind_cap_sec bounds how far a rate may be carried, so a session that merely sat idle cannot pause on the passage of time. Both defaults changed after the 2026-08-19 sensor-freeze incident (headroom 12 -> 20, time anchoring added): a subagent fan-out burned 27 points in 8 minutes while the sensor was frozen, and the old arithmetic measured the span to `now`, so the rate decayed to nothing exactly when it was needed. See docs/sensor-freeze-report-2026-08-19.md.
_staleness_comment: Brink reads usage from the state file the statusline writes, and the statusline only refreshes on main-session activity. Work that burns tokens away from the main conversation (a background workflow, a large subagent fan-out) can leave that reading frozen while the real usage climbs. When a reading is older than max_age_sec, Brink says so instead of trusting it. It never pauses on age alone - a stale reading cannot tell anyone the real number - so this is a warning, not a gate.
_reset_ping_comment: Ping when a window rolls over (budget is back). 'enabled' off for 5h (resets several times a day = noise) / on for weekly (days of budget back). 'floor' = only ping if you were at/above this % before it reset, so a reset from low usage stays silent.
_resume_comment: Opt-in. skip_permissions=true relaunches with --dangerously-skip-permissions: the resumed agent runs WITHOUT permission prompts, unattended, in your project. Leave false unless you fully accept that. max_chain = safety cap on consecutive auto-resumes per session (a runaway task must not burn every window for days unattended); 0 = unlimited. in_place = win32-only: resume by injecting a continue prompt into the same window instead of relaunching a new one; only an explicit boolean true keeps it on. continue_prompt = the text typed into the resumed session; it must not start with / ! @ # and must not contain a newline (TUI-unsafe input falls back to the default prompt).

resume.continue_prompt: The usage limit has reset. Continue the task you paused before the pause - do not redo finished work.

_watchdog_comment: Opt-in, win32-only. Revives sessions whose PROCESS died mid-turn (terminal closed, crash, reboot) - no usage pause needed; this covers what scheduled resume can't. Turn on with `brink watchdog on` (also registers+starts the hidden logon daemon; `brink watchdog off` reverses everything). mode: off = feature dark (hooks exit immediately) | ask = toast only, revive manually with `brink revive` | auto = headless-revive after cancel_window_seconds (abort with `brink cancel`). max_revives_per_hour = global backstop across all sessions (0 = unlimited); revives also count toward resume.max_chain per session, and resume.skip_permissions applies to the revived run. revive_prompt has the same guards as continue_prompt.

watchdog.revive_prompt: This session was terminated unexpectedly while work was in progress. Review the recent conversation and continue the task - do not redo finished work.
